In competitive exams like SSC CGL, IBPS PO, SBI Clerk, and CDS, Subject-Verb Agreement is responsible for nearly 25% of all error-spotting questions. Written by a senior English Grammar educator with 22 years of classroom experience and 15+ years of competitive coaching, this book breaks down all 36 granular agreement principles tested across SSC and Banking examinations over the last two decades. You will learn the exact psychological traps examiners engineer and how to bypass them in under 15 seconds.

What You Will Learn

  • ✓ The Prepositional Blindfold Rule: Instantly isolate the true syntactic subject from lengthy interrupting modifiers and parenthetical clauses.
  • ✓ The Proximity Trap Matrix: Master correlative conjunctions (either...or, neither...nor, not only...but also) without confusing nearest-noun rules with subject-head rules.
  • ✓ Collective Noun Polarization: Distinguish when collective nouns (committee, jury, audience, staff) take singular verbs vs. plural verbs in divided opinions.
  • ✓ Indefinite Pronoun Algorithms: Clear all ambiguity around each, every, none of, one of the, and relative clause antecedents.
  • ✓ Inverted Sentence Parsing: Uncover concealed subjects placed after the verb in locative and conditional constructions.

Who This Book Is For

Specially engineered for candidates preparing for SSC CGL (Tier 1 & Tier 2), SSC CHSL, IBPS PO/Clerk, SBI PO, CDS, NDA, and State Public Service Commissions who score well on reading comprehension but repeatedly lose 0.25 to 0.50 negative marks on deceptive error-spotting sentences.

Why This Book Is Different

Standard school grammar textbooks teach Subject-Verb Agreement through simple 5-word examples ("The boy runs / The boys run"). In actual competitive exams, question setters never give you simple sentences; they pad sentences with 15-word prepositional modifiers to distance the head noun from the verb.

This guide equips you with Elimination Matrices and 200+ exam-calibrated drill problems taken directly from the difficulty distribution of Tier-1 and Tier-2 examination sets.

Sample Exam Questions & Analysis

Question 1 (SSC CGL Pattern)

The quality of the freshly harvested organic apples exported to several European countries (A) / are exceptionally high (B) / according to the international inspection committee. (C) / No error (D)

Error in Part (B): Replace are with is.
Examiner Trap Explained: The plural noun apples and countries immediately precede the verb, tempting the candidate into an auditory proximity error. The true subject is the singular abstract noun quality.
Question 2 (IBPS PO Pattern)

He is one of those dedicated research scholars who (A) / has worked tirelessly on the vaccine trial (B) / without seeking any commercial publicity. (C) / No error (D)

Error in Part (B): Replace has worked with have worked.
Examiner Trap Explained: In the construction one of those + plural noun + who/that, the relative pronoun refers back to the plural antecedent scholars, requiring a plural verb.

Rather than listing standard conjugations tables that you can find in any elementary schoolbook, this guide organizes tenses around Exam Distractor Patterns. It highlights the specific adverbs and temporal connectors examiners use as bait to trigger erroneous choices.

Sample Exam Questions & Analysis

Question 1 (SSC CGL 2023)

The chief engineer has submitted the final project feasibility report (A) / to the municipal commissioner (B) / two weeks ago. (C) / No error (D)

Error in Part (A): Replace has submitted with submitted.
Examiner Trap Explained: The adverbial time phrase two weeks ago specifies a closed, completed historical moment in the past. Present Perfect cannot combine with past-specific time markers.
Question 2 (Banking PO Pattern)

If the authorities had taken precautionary measures in time, (A) / the catastrophic flooding in the lower valley (B) / could have been avoided. (C) / No error (D)

Result: (D) No error.
Analysis: This tests Third Conditional syntax: If + past perfect (had taken) paired with modal perfect passive (could have been avoided) in the main result clause.

Sample Exam Questions & Analysis

Question 1 (SSC CGL Tier-2 Actual Exam)

The teacher said to the students, "The earth revolves around the sun."

Correct Indirect Form: The teacher told the students that the earth revolves around the sun.
Examiner Trap Explained: Students often mistakenly backshift revolves into revolved. Because this is a permanent cosmic/scientific fact, the present tense is strictly retained.
Question 2 (Interrogative Pattern)

Examiner Trap Explained: Candidates frequently write "where did I live" retaining question word order, or add an incorrect that ("asked me that where..."). In indirect speech, the clause becomes an affirmative statement.

The panel members discussed about the financial crisis (A) / for nearly four hours (B) / before reaching a consensus. (C) / No error (D)

Error in Part (A): Remove about.

Sample Exam Questions & Analysis

Question 1 (Gerund Possessive Rule)

The management objected to him arriving late (A) / at every critical board meeting (B) / without prior intimation. (C) / No error (D)

Error in Part (A): Replace him with his.
Examiner Trap Explained: Arriving functions here as a gerund (verbal noun). A noun or pronoun modifying a gerund must be in the possessive case (his arriving).
Question 2 (Dangling Participle Trap)

Walking along the riverbank on Sunday morning, (A) / a venomous snake bit him (B) / on his right ankle. (C) / No error (D)

Error in Part (A): The participial phrase lacks an appropriate logical subject.
Correction: While he was walking along the riverbank... As written, the sentence implies that the snake was walking along the riverbank.
